title: No frame of a 50 track zoom is held up by the system's drawing cleanup
goal: Zooming the timeline of a 50 track edit is smooth but for a rare single frame, about one in 3,000, that takes 20 to 58 milliseconds and reads as a tiny hitch. Every frame of a zoom should be as smooth as the rest.
notes: Split off an-edit-with-50-tracks-and-100-clips-scrolls-pla (its acceptance: what is not reached is filed, one cost each). Measure: a walk with setup {"forget":["all"],"wideEdit":50}, wait 3, then {"do":"speed","measure":"timeline","form":"long"} six times and {"do":"wait","seconds":90,"onTheClock":true}; profile it with Scripts/perf/pass-profile.sh <walk> then Scripts/perf/pass-profile.py /tmp/photonz-pass-sampler --waits. Caught 2026-11-25, two of two: 'PASS 139 zoom out held | 38.9' and 'PASS 576 near fit fresh | 31.6'. Main thread: CA::Transaction::run_commit_handlers -> _dispatch_sync_f_slow on RenderBox's queue (27 looks of the first on CoreAnimation's own mutex in CA::Context::commit_transaction). Holder in both, a dispatch worker: RB::SharedSurfaceGroup::prune_removed_locked -> test_markers -> RB::CommitMarker::Observer::test_displayed -> -[CAContext waitForCommitId:timeout:] -> CA::Context::ping / wait_for_synchronize -> mach_msg, 27 to 36 ms, that is the window server. No app code on it. The only lead: that cleanup runs when drawings that share a surface (RBLayer, SwiftUI Canvas and drawn text) go away or change size, so fewer drawings coming and going in a zoom (held paintings as plain CGImage layers, no Canvas) should mean fewer cleanups. Not tried.
acceptance: Over ten runs of the timeline measure on the 50 track edit (about 17,000 frames), no frame holds the main thread over 16 ms (today: 21 ms once, 33 ms once, 58 ms once in eleven runs, unprofiled)
No change in what the timeline draws: film of a zoom in, out and near Fit before and after, opened and compared, none blank
Zoom and scroll p95 stay under 8.3 ms and the edits under 16 ms in Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --wide 50
If the hold cannot be avoided from the app, the audit says so with what was tried, and the task is dropped with that rather than worked round at a cost a person would see

Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after numbers. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Triage 2026-11-26: two other focus tasks end on what may be the same hold. The hour-long timeline (pass 26) has a 30 ms main thread frame in about 1,500, unprofiled; the scrub task (pass 3) has an 8 ms wait in mach_msg inside CA::Context::commit_transaction at the start of each drag. If this task finds a way round the hold, check both; if it finds none, say so for all three.

From the scrub task, pass 4 (2026-11-26): its start-of-drag hold was not this one. It was set off by the scrub sound's AVAudioEngine.start() and went away when the engine was started before the drag; the main thread blocked in its own commit send, not on RenderBox's queue. So the scrub task no longer shares this cause.
